items.title: A verse that does not exist
items.note: Romans 8 has 39 verses. parseReference reads the verse number and throws it away, so only the chapter is range-checked.

items.title: A verse range running off the end of the chapter
items.note: Same gap. The dash after a colon is read as a verse range, and verse numbers are never bounded.

items.title: A real key term, attached to the wrong book
items.note: That term is indexed under John. checkTerms looks it up globally and never asks whether it belongs to the book in the reference.

items.title: A real episode, filed under the wrong chapter of the right book
items.note: That episode is Romans 4. checkEvents matches the name and the era but never compares the episode's own chapter ref to the item's reference.

items.title: A real person of the book, in a chapter they never appear in
items.note: Adam is in Romans, chapter 5. checkPeople scopes to the book, not to the chapter, because booksAppearing is the finest grain the index has.

items.note: Every structured field here is true, so the item passes. The false claim is in the title, which nothing reads. This one is not fixable from the index and is the honest limit of the approach.
